A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe the same QNPG work, with corresponding algorithms, equations, and Appendices A–F. Text and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports algorithm construction and theoretical convergence and query-complexity bounds. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–F report original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 retains the theoretical study and proof appendices, without reporting original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The truncated estimators, quantum variance reduction, and policy updates are unchanged. v3 removes Algorithm 1's unused 'x0, v0 ← 0' line; neither variable participates in subsequent computation.

E1.justification: Both study the same infinite-horizon discounted MDP setting theoretically. Neither uses datasets or benchmark tasks for training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline experiments. The theoretical comparisons with classical NPG and existing quantum optimization methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. No experimental splits, metrics, budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. The appendices retain the same mathematical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The analytical estimator-variance guarantees are unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version. The reported theoretical bounds, including the O-tilde(ε^-1.5) query complexity and O(ε^-1) iteration complexity in Theorem 3, are retained.

T1.justification: The definitions, Assumptions 1–3, Theorems 1–3, Lemmas 1–7, and proofs in Appendices A–F retain the same mathematical content. Apparent extraction differences in mathematical symbols resolve to equivalent rendered equations.

C1.justification: Both retain the same novelty claims, quantum model-free NPG contribution, bounded truncation bias, and claimed O-tilde(ε^-1.5) quantum query complexity versus the classical O-tilde(ε^-2) bound.

C2.justification: The explanations of truncation bias, quantum inner-loop acceleration, and the classical outer-loop bottleneck are unchanged. The qualifications concerning nonconvexity and future actor–critic and constrained-RL extensions are also retained.

D1.justification: The oracle constructions in Appendix A, variance-reduction subroutines in Appendix B, and learning-rate and truncation prescriptions are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, or code/data access disclosures are added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Ganguly et al. switches from its ICML 2025 citation to its 2023 preprint, and Gaur et al. from ICML 2024 to its 2024 preprint; the corresponding titles identify the same works.

P1.justification: The running header corrects 'Quantum MPG' to 'Quantum NPG', Algorithm 1 loses an unused initialization line, and bibliographic metadata is edited. The substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Typesetting changes line wrapping, equation spacing, and page breaks. Algorithm 1's display is shortened and its lines renumbered. The same three algorithm displays remain; neither version contains figures or data tables.

improvement.justification: Removing the unexplained, unused initialization in Algorithm 1 and correcting the running header slightly improve clarity and consistency. The scientific claims, guarantees, and appendix proofs remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to presentation.
